Surah 112 = al-Ikhlas (الإخلاص), meaning 'Sincerity/purity of devotion'; 112th in the mushaf; 4 ayat; juz 30

Reason for the name (Qurtubi): the hadith that it equals a third of the Quran / Allah made it one part of three (Muslim 811b) - 'bi-hadha al-ma'na summiyat Surat al-Ikhlas, wallahu a'lam'. ONE tafseer source only; do not state as certain

Makki/Madani: IKHTILAAF. Makki: Ibn Kathir ('wa hiya makkiyya'), Qurtubi first view (Ibn Mas'ud, Hasan, 'Ata', 'Ikrima, Jabir), Ma'ariful Qur'an (same names), Tanzil/fawazahmed0 metadata. Madani: one of Ibn 'Abbas' two reports, Qatada, Dahhak, Suddi (Qurtubi; Ma'ariful Qur'an for Qatada, Dahhak)

Order of revelation: NOT found in any source opened today (Tanzil chapters/fawazahmed0 info have no field). Do not say a number in the video until a PC check of an accepted list (e.g. Tanzil quran-data / Cairo list)
Other names of the surah: none found in IK/Qurtubi/Tabari/MQ text opened today. Do not claim any; PC check (e.g. Qurtubi/Suyuti list) if the script wants one
Main message: pure tawheed - Allah is One, besought of all, no child, no parent, no equal; refutes every kind of shirk and wrong idea about Allah's nature

SHAN-E-NUZUL: all reports are of disputed grade. Main one: the mushrikin said 'O Muhammad, name your Lord's lineage' (Ubayy ibn Ka'b via Abu al-'Aliya; Ahmad 5/133, Tirmidhi 3364, Tabari). Ibn Kathir: Tirmidhi also gave it as mursal and said 'this (mursal) is more correct'; Qurtubi: same ('hadha asahh'). Tirmidhi 3364 grades: Shakir hasan, Albani hasan, Zubair Ali Za'i da'if. Other reports (Jews asked 'who created Allah', or gold/silver/copper; Tabari, Qurtubi, MQ) are mursal/without isnad. = NO sahih-grade shan-e-nuzul

facts.claim: Safe script line (user decides): 'सूरह के उतरने का कोई सहीह-दर्जे का ख़ास वाक़िया नहीं मिलता। तफ़्सीरों में एक रिवायत आती है कि लोगों ने अल्लाह के बारे में सवाल किए और जवाब में ये सूरह उतरी - पर इस रिवायत की सनद पर उलमा में इख़्तिलाफ़ है।' Makki/Madani line from P3

SAHIH: a man heard another repeating 'Qul huwa Allahu ahad'; next morning he told the Prophet SAW as if he thought it little; the Prophet said: by Him in Whose Hand is my life, it equals a third of the Quran. Bukhari 5013 (also 7374); Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. Cited by Ibn Kathir and Qurtubi

SAHIH: 'Can any of you not recite a third of the Quran in a night?' - hard for them - 'Who can?' - 'Allah the One, As-Samad is a third of the Quran'. Bukhari 5015 (Abu Sa'id); Muslim 811a (Abu al-Darda': 'Qul huwa Allahu ahad is equal to a third')

SAHIH: Abu Hurairah - the Prophet SAW said 'gather, I will recite a third of the Quran', came out, recited the surah, went in; then said 'it is equal to a third of the Quran'. Muslim 812a/812b. (Cited Tirmidhi + Ma'ariful Qur'an + Qurtubi)

SAHIH: 'A'isha - a man commanding an expedition always ended the recitation with Qul huwa Allahu ahad; asked why: 'it is the attribute (sifat) of Ar-Rahman and I love to recite it'; the Prophet SAW: 'tell him Allah loves him'. Bukhari 7375; Muslim 813; Ibn Kathir (Book of Tawhid), Qurtubi

SAHIH (optional, a report only - no ruling): 'A'isha - each night at bedtime the Prophet SAW cupped his hands, recited Ikhlas, Falaq, Nas, blew, wiped his body, three times. Bukhari 5017 (also 5748); Tirmidhi 3402 (Zubair: 'Sahih Bukhari'); Ibn Kathir

Meaning of 'equal to a third': Qurtubi gives two views (the name As-Samad is unique to this surah; the Quran is thirds - ahkam, wa'd/wa'id, names&attributes - and this surah holds the third part) quoting Muslim 811b 'Allah divided the Quran into three parts, one part is Qul huwa Allahu ahad'. Treat as explanation (ikhtilaaf in reasoning); DO NOT say it replaces reciting the Quran or gives the reward of a full khatm

112:1 - 'Qul' is a command to the Prophet SAW to convey; 'huwa Allahu ahad': Allah is One - single, no partner, no peer, no equal; 'ahad' is stronger than 'wahid' (beyond composition, plurality, likeness). Ibn Kathir, Qurtubi, Ma'ariful Qur'an, Tabari agree on the core

112:2 - As-Samad: the One to whom all turn for their needs, who needs no one (Ibn 'Abbas via Dahhak in Qurtubi and 'Ikrima via Ibn Kathir; Ma'ariful Qur'an quoting Ibn Kathir/Tabarani; Tabari: the sayyid to whom people turn, none above). Other quoted senses (perfect in every honour/knowledge; ever-lasting) fit the same core

112:3 - He has no child and no parent (Ibn Kathir: no child, parent or spouse; Ma'ariful Qur'an: no child, nor child of anyone; Qurtubi: Ubayy/Ibn 'Abbas - not born and not begetting; nothing born but dies, nothing dies but leaves inheritance, and Allah neither dies nor is inherited from)

112:4 - none is equal/like Him (kufuwan = like, equal in rank/attributes/works). Ibn Kathir (none similar, equal; Mujahid: no spouse), Qurtubi (no like, no equal, 'nothing is like Him'), Ma'ariful Qur'an

Ma'ariful Qur'an: the surah denies every wrong idea in turn (no God at all / not necessary being / no perfect attributes / many gods / helpers besides Him / children). Ibn Kathir (via 'Ikrima): revealed when Jews, Christians, fire/sun-worshippers and idol-worshippers each claimed otherwise - tabi'i statement, NOT for the video as shan-e-nuzul
